$comment: What each COMMITTED DERIVED artifact was made from, recorded as a content
hash of its inputs, so `bun run derive:check` can answer whether it still
describes the bytes it was derived from.
It sits beside config/tools.json rather than inside it because the two answer
different questions about the same pipeline. tools.json asks whether the
avifenc on this machine is the one that baked the library. This asks whether
the library still matches what was baked FROM it. A tool can be perfectly
pinned while every artifact downstream of it is nine days stale, which is
exactly what happened (gotcha 46).
WHY A GRAPH RATHER THAN ANOTHER TRIPWIRE. Four incidents here share one
shape: a content-addressed input moved and something derived from it did not.
#394 re-encoded 316 thumbnails and re-baked no histograms. An /a/ asset
changing hash orphans every a-dict snapshot naming the old one. The search
index froze twice. Each bought one bespoke check, and each bespoke check was
written to catch the incident that had already happened. This is the general
form, and adding an artifact to it is a data edit rather than a new script.
THE CHECK NEVER RUNS A GENERATOR AND NEVER MUTATES THE TREE. That is a
requirement rather than a nicety: several agents work in this repo at once, so
a check that rebuilds artifacts in place would be writing over somebody else's
uncommitted work. It also has to answer from a clean checkout, and the three
families that actually go stale cannot be rebuilt from one (images/meta/ is a
local pipeline artifact, metadata.json reads the SOOC originals, the og cards
capture production). Hashing inputs works on all of them; rebuilding works on
none of them.
TIERS. `pinned` means the inputs are committed bytes, so the recorded digest
is checkable here with no tool and no network. `unverifiable` means the inputs
are not in this repository, and the entry says which ones and why. An
unverifiable entry is reported as a note and never counted as a pass, on the
same reasoning as the two tools in tools.json that report no version: a check
whose summary line covers more than the check does is worse than one that says
what it skipped.
`tools` names entries in config/tools.json whose `recorded` version is part of
an artifact's identity, so swapping encoders reads as staleness. A FIRST-PARTY
tool needs no such entry, because its source is committed and goes straight
into `inputs`, with ONE exception worth knowing before adding another. The
histogram bake's tool inputs (zenc's sources and Cargo.lock) are NOT in its
digest, because that artifact can be reproduced from committed bytes alone, and
CI does exactly that: `bun run histograms:check` re-bakes it and compares it to
the committed file. A measured output beats a hashed input, and the hash made
every zenc dependency bump read as stale until somebody re-baked by hand.
WHAT IS DELIBERATELY NOT HERE, so the coverage claim stays honest:
- the MCP server cards, which a contract test already deep-equals against
each server's live tools/list. That is stronger than a digest, and a second
check over the same artifact is a second thing to keep in agreement.
- src/dict/a-dict and p-dict, whose input is what production served rather
than anything in the tree. dcz:check owns the question they actually raise,
which is coverage of the live shell rather than freshness against a source.
- images/fingerprints.json and images/exif.json, which had entries here until
2026-08-29 and are BUILD OUTPUT now. build.ts step 1a derives both into
.build/public on every deploy, so neither can be stale by construction and
there is nothing left in the tree for a digest to describe. Note what that
costs and what it does not: public/i keeps its pinned digest through
images/hashes, which declares the identical inputs, so dropping the
fingerprints entry took no coverage of the pixel tiers with it.
SET MODE AND `covers`, and why the second one is the half that bites. An
artifact keyed by stem does not depend on the pixel bytes: re-encoding a photo
does not change what is in the picture, so pinning alt.json to bytes would
report it stale on every re-encode and teach somebody to re-record it without
looking. `set` projects each input path to a key and digests the key SET
instead, so those artifacts go stale for the one reason they can be: a photo
arrived or left.
That reason is not always the only one, and assuming it was cost a blind spot.
semantics.json also folds in each caption and recipe, so a re-captioned photo
left it stale while its stem set, and its digest, never moved. `bytes` hashes
such whole-file inputs beside a set (set mode only). The way to find them is to
read what the generator OPENS rather than what its declaration assumes: on
2026-09-22 strace over the regenerate commands found this one in one run.
The digest alone is still not enough for an artifact built one key at a time. A
resumable generator that dies halfway leaves a file covering most of the set,
and --lock afterwards would call it fresh forever. `covers` reads the output and
asserts it HAS an entry per input, computed live rather than recorded, so it is
the one verdict --lock cannot clear. It found semantics.json at 158 of 165 on
the day it was written.

derivations.why: images/hashes.json maps each stem to the hash8 of its four tiers, and buildImagesManifest bakes those into the manifest's absolute URLs. A stem missing from it is skipped rather than served broken, so the failure of a stale map is a photo that quietly stops appearing in the grid.

THE ONE THIS FILE WAS BUILT FOR. images/histograms.json holds four 64-bin channels per photo, baked by `zenc histogram` from the SHIPPED hashed JPG tier, and build.ts derives the served /images/meta/<stem>.json from it. #394 re-encoded 316 of those JPEGs on 2026-08-14 and re-baked nothing, so the bars described pixels nobody had been served for nine days. photos:check could not see it, because it compares histograms.json against images/meta/, which the build derives FROM histograms.json: two sides of one source agree no matter what the pixels say. zenc's sources and Cargo.lock were inputs here until 2026-09-28 and are not now: CI's native photo validation job runs `bun run histograms:check`, which re-bakes every photo with the zenc the tree builds and compares the result to this file byte for byte. That measures the output a tool change could move, where the digest could only say it MIGHT have moved, and it cost a hand re-bake and --lock on every zenc bump (#871, #985). public/i stays, so a re-encode that skips the bake still fails here with no cargo.
derivations.regenerate: tools/photos/zenc/target/release/zenc histogram --root public && bun tools/photos/build-histogram-index.ts (inside a photo add: bash tools/photos/extract-photo-metadata.sh "$SOOC_DIR")

derivations.why: images/alt.json is the AI caption per photo, and it is ALT TEXT first: a photo with no entry ships to a screen reader with nothing to say. photos:check already fails on an uncaptioned stem, so what this adds is the other direction, a caption still carried for a photo that has been deleted.

images/semantics.json widens what queryPhotos can match beyond the one-sentence caption and the EXIF. A photo missing from it is still findable, one tier down, which is why it went unnoticed: the failure is a search result that is quietly worse rather than an error. FOUND STALE BY THIS CHECK at 158 of 165, because gen-photo-semantics.ts had been reading a www/ that the 2026-08-18 split deleted, so nobody had been able to run it since. The stem set is not its only input: the generator folds each caption (alt.json) and Fuji recipe (metadata.json) into the terms, so both are hashed whole under `bytes`. Until 2026-09-22 they were undeclared, and a re-captioned photo left semantics.json describing the old caption while this entry read fresh; strace found the reads and one changed caption proved the gap.
derivations.regenerate: bun tools/photos/gen-photo-semantics.ts   # add --vision for the model tier

derivations.why: gen-desktop-partial.ts projects shell-data.ts (pins, profiles, icons, tray art) and site-manifest.json (which routes are taskbar applications) into a checked-in Worker partial, the icon sprite, and the per-section favicons. All of it is committed, on both sides, so this is fully checkable. Staleness here is silent by construction: the old partial keeps rendering a taskbar perfectly, it just describes a site that has moved on.
images/metadata.json is the EXIF record keyed by stem, plus the Fujifilm recipe card, read by exif-sooc from the camera originals.
derivations.unverifiable: The inputs are the SOOC originals, which live in R2 and in one local folder rather than in this repository, so no checkout can hash them. What is checkable about this family is that every published stem carries a record, which photos:check already asserts. images/exif.json USED TO BE A SECOND OUTPUT HERE and is build output as of 2026-08-29: build.ts step 1a projects it out of metadata.json through the 22-pair key map, so there is no committed copy left to go stale and nothing for this graph to record.

derivations.why: The /pixel-peeper trial set: 320px tiles cropped at native resolution from the source photos, encoded on one byte budget per trial, and a manifest of the trials that cleared their axis's legibility gate. Regenerated whole; the manifest is all-or-nothing.
derivations.unverifiable: gen-pixel-peeper.ts reads the SOOC originals in the photo source folder, which is outside the tree, and its crop selection is a scored scan whose answer depends on the scorer's exact arithmetic. There is no committed input to hash; the set is a deliberate act, and the generator refuses to write unless at least 12 trials survive.

derivations.why: One pre-baked 1200x630 card per garage and lwe page, each showing that page's live demo on the Bliss desktop, so a shared link unfurls as the interaction rather than a bare title.
derivations.unverifiable: gen-og-cards.ts drives Chrome against PRODUCTION so the demos carry live data, which makes the input a deployed site at a moment in time rather than any bytes in the tree. Pinning these to their page sources would be a lie in the useful direction: the card can go stale from a deploy that changed no page file at all.

derivations.why: public/lwe/quadgrams.txt is the 4000-row English quadgram rank table the /lwe/vigenere solver hill-climbs against, cut down from a 46,040-row model to keep a demo nobody has clicked yet from costing more than nav.js and luna.css together.
derivations.unverifiable: The input is buttcrack's english_quadgrams.txt (MIT), pinned at commit c398ef10, the one commit that has touched that file: 46,040 rows, 369,469 bytes, sha256 10970728a2367936eb70532b7013593e214cc195b97026fc38d5ddf9c0707704. It is not in this repository because derive:check reads no network, so this stays unverifiable HERE and verifiable on demand: the regenerate command fetches that pinned file, refuses it unless the sha256 matches, and rebuilds the table. Run 2026-10-01, it reproduced the committed public/lwe/quadgrams.txt byte for byte. What derive:check cannot see is a regeneration from some other corpus, which is what the hash in the command is for. FOUND BROKEN while taking this census: the generator wrote to `../lwe/quadgrams.txt` relative to tools/photos/, which is tools/lwe/, a directory that has never existed. Gotcha 40 again, third instance in one afternoon.
derivations.regenerate: f="${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/english_quadgrams.txt" && curl -sfL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/0xdiid/buttcrack/c398ef10b5810f14e3065f9addea871bce028ffe/src/buttcrack/data/english_quadgrams.txt -o "$f" && echo "10970728a2367936eb70532b7013593e214cc195b97026fc38d5ddf9c0707704  $f" | shasum -a 256 -c && bun tools/photos/gen-quadgram-table.ts "$f"

derivations.why: The GitHub social preview for this repository, 1280x640, two variants.
derivations.unverifiable: It drives Chrome against the LIVE homepage, and that page draws a random 12 of 158 photos per request, so the generator's own header says every regeneration ships a different grid. There is no digest to record: the same inputs deliberately do not produce the same bytes. Same class as og/cards.

derivations.why: The resto-mod reference photos the car-link tooltips draw, as the dual AVIF and JPG pair those tooltips expect. No EXIF, no R2, no hashed tier: they are illustrations rather than photographs of the library.
derivations.unverifiable: The input is a reference photo from somewhere on the web, credited by hand in public/cars/CREDITS.txt and not in this repository. There is nothing to hash. What is checkable is that each stem has both tiers and a credit line, which belongs with the page contract rather than here.

derivations.why: The sample set the /garage/encoding study compares, one file per encoder and quality point, plus the byte counts the page quotes.
derivations.unverifiable: The inputs are source images held outside this repository and SEVEN external encoders at whatever version the machine has. config/tools.json records those versions and is the right place to ask whether they moved; a digest here would restate that without adding anything, because the source images can never be hashed from a checkout.

$comment: Every file that WRITES is classified exactly once, so a generator nobody
declared cannot exist quietly. config/derivations.json answers 'is this
artifact stale' and could not answer the question underneath it: whether an
artifact has a declaration at all. That is the gap gotcha 46 fell through,
since histograms.json had no declaration and so there was nothing for a check
to be wrong about.
A file here is either named by some derivation's `regenerate` command, or it
is exempt WITH A REASON. A new generator is covered by existing rather than by
somebody remembering, which is the property worth copying from tools.json.
The scanner reads JS, TS and Python and NOT shell; the limit and its reasoning
TWO SCANNERS. JS, TS and Python get an exact scan, because a write is a named
call. Shell gets a deliberately wider one: does the script MENTION a committed
path at all. That over-approximates, which fails closed, so a script that only
reads still has to be classified and says so. A shell script handed its target
as an argument is invisible to it, and that is the same reason perf-snapshot.ts
is exempt: a tool that writes where it is told has no fixed artifact to pin.
The reasoning is at the top of tools/lib/derive-writers.ts.

exempt.tools/build.ts: writes only into .build/, the staged tree, which is rebuilt from source every deploy and never committed
exempt.tools/served-manifest.ts: writes served-manifest.json, a CI artifact cut from .build/public on each push to main and signed there; it is never committed, and tools/check-served.ts is what compares it against production
exempt.tools/lib/hash-client-assets.ts: build step 6's core, called by build.ts with the staged root: writes only the /a/ copies and the repointed loaders under the directory it is handed, which is .build/ in a build and a temp dir in the contract suite
exempt.tools/bake-worker-pages.ts: build step 5b, spawned by build.ts in its own process: writes only the baked Worker pages into .build/public, the staged tree
exempt.tools/gen-md-twins.ts: same, a build step: the twins are generated into .build/ precisely so no committed copy can fall behind
exempt.tools/generate-search-index.ts: same, and for the same reason: it was committed until 2026-08-24 and froze twice, which is why it is build output now
exempt.tools/gen-runtime-types.ts: writes only gitignored files: config/.generated/ (the shared runtime declarations and cf-garage's cache key) and, through `wrangler build --x-new-config --x-cf-build-output` in cf-garage/, cf-garage/.cloudflare/ (its generated Env plus runtime types, and the build output tree that comes with them, keyed on the wrangler version and cloudflare.config.ts). For config/.generated/workers-runtime.d.ts: the Workers runtime declarations, a pure function of the wrangler pin (which pins workerd) and the config bytes, both of which its first line keys on so a stale file regenerates itself. Nothing committed can fall behind it, which is the same argument as the two build steps above, run at typecheck time instead of deploy time
exempt.tools/gen-mcp-cards.ts: the cards ARE committed, and a contract test deep-equals each one against its server's live tools/list. That is stronger than a digest, and a second check over one artifact is a second thing to keep in agreement
exempt.tools/gen-dotfiles.ts: public/dotfiles/macos.sh IS committed, and contract-dotfiles-script-matches-the-page.test.mjs holds it byte-equal to the page data through the same renderer, the mcp-cards argument: a test over the artifact is stronger than a digest over its inputs
exempt.tools/gen-manifest.ts: writes the nav fences and the Worker's registry module, which build.ts invariant #8 verifies against config/site-manifest.json on every build
exempt.tools/roll-shell-dictionary.ts: writes src/dict/, whose input is what production SERVED rather than anything in this tree. dcz:check owns the question those raise, which is coverage of the live shell
exempt.tools/lib/page-family.ts: the roll's one writer of src/dict/f-dict, the committed site-page dictionary. Its input is either what production SERVED or the fresh corpus the build derived from the final staged pages, and neither is anything in this tree: build.ts reads the file back and ships it while it is within drift. dcz:check reports when production and f-dict disagree, and contract-family-dictionary-is-committed.test.mjs holds the file well-formed and singular
exempt.pipelines/garage/generate.mjs: an AUTHORING tool: it writes a page into src/pages that a human then edits by hand, so there is no input it stays a pure function of
exempt.pipelines/lwe/generate.mjs: an AUTHORING tool, like its garage twin: it writes an LWE conversation page into src/pages that a human then edits by hand, so there is no input it stays a pure function of
exempt.pipelines/lwe/build-corpus.mjs: an AUTHORING tool too, writing the retrieval passages into lwe-ask/src/passages.ts, which is then edited in place rather than regenerated
exempt.tools/photos/inject-og-meta.ts: same, a one-time edit that adds og:image tags to pages people then keep editing
exempt.tools/check-derivations.ts: writes this file and its lock, which is the graph recording itself
exempt.tools/check-checkpoints.ts: --sync writes src/worker/checkpoints.json, the deploy-log projection, which checkpoints:check already diffs against D1
exempt.tools/typecheck.ts: --update writes the typecheck ratchet baseline, a machine-owned record of owed errors
exempt.tools/perf-snapshot.ts: writes a snapshot file named on the command line, never a fixed committed path
exempt.tools/dependency-snapshot.ts: --out writes the dependency submission body to a path named on the command line, which dependency-snapshot.yml posts and discards; it commits nothing
exempt.tools/conflict-triage.ts: --html writes a conflict view to a path named on the command line, for a person to read once; it commits nothing and derives nothing
exempt.tools/lib/bun-gates.ts: the gates bump-bun-pin.ts and canary-bun.ts share: it unzips a candidate bun into a work directory, mirrors the manifests to resolve a lockfile with each runtime, and builds twice, parking the pinned `.build/` in `.build.pinned-baseline` while the candidate builds and putting it back in a finally. Nothing it writes is committed
exempt.tools/bump-wrangler-pin.ts: writes an optional canary JSON report to the caller's path and rewrites the wrangler line of the root package.json to a newer pkg.pr.new commit URL and relocks, the same maintenance edit to a hand-authored file that lib/bun-pin.ts makes for packageManager; check-wrangler.ts holds the URL, bun.lock and the installed version together after every move
exempt.tools/canary-bun.ts: writes the JSON report the canary workflow files an issue from, into a path the caller names; every other write is bun-gates.ts's and is listed there
exempt.tools/bump-bun-pin.ts: writes the JSON report bun-pin.yml files its one issue from, into a path the caller names with --json; the pin itself goes through lib/bun-pin.ts's writePin and every gate's scratch writes are bun-gates.ts's, both listed here
exempt.tools/canary-wrangler.ts: writes into a detached worktree it creates in the temp directory and removes in a finally (the candidate wrangler's install, its dry-run bundle), plus the pinned dry-run's bundle beside it and the JSON report the caller names. Nothing under the repository moves except `.build/`, which the pinned dry-run re-stages with the pinned toolchain exactly as `validate` does
exempt.tools/canary-browsers.ts: writes the JSON report the canary workflow files an issue from, into a path the caller names, and nothing else; the page it reads is loaded over file://, and the two live probes beside it only READ production (a dictionary exchange and a data-URI decode)
exempt.tools/lib/upstream-watches.ts: the LIST of upstream watches, which is a record rather than an artifact; the two CSS watches carry `Bun.write` inside their probe scripts, which timbrado's runner executes in a mkdtemp directory it removes, so nothing under the repository is touched
exempt.tools/workerd-zstd-probe.ts: writes a two-file probe Worker into a mkdtemp directory, boots it through wrangler's createTestHarness, and removes the directory in a finally; its one output is a JSON line on stdout that canary-wrangler.ts reads
exempt.tools/workerd-temporal-probe.ts: writes a two-file probe Worker into a mkdtemp directory, boots it through wrangler's createTestHarness under the site's compatibility date and flags, and removes the directory in a finally; its one output is a JSON line on stdout that canary-wrangler.ts reads
exempt.tools/lib/bun-pin.ts: writes config/bun-pin.json, rewriting ONLY its `bun` pin (it was package.json's packageManager until 2026-09-15), which is a maintenance edit to a hand-authored file rather than a derived artifact. contract-the-bun-pin-is-declared-once.test.mjs holds that pin and its three readers together. THIS ENTRY FIRST SAID IT WROTE A TEMP RELEASE ZIP, which is bump-bun-pin.ts and not this: the census caught the file correctly and the reason beside it was wrong, which is the failure mode an exemption list has
exempt.tools/check-infra.ts: writes one request line into a mkdtemp directory while probing the edge
exempt.tools/lens-seed.ts: writes seed captures into a scratch directory
exempt.tools/photos/codec-knob-probe.ts: writes scratch encodes and an optional --json report while measuring cjxl, avifenc and AV2 (avifenc-avm) flags at matched bytes, and commits nothing
exempt.tools/photos/avif-chroma-probe.ts: writes scratch tiers, encodes and an optional --json report while comparing AVIF chroma layouts at the shipped bytes, and commits nothing
exempt.tools/bump-deps.ts: with --write, rewrites exact pins in the package.json manifests, relocks bun.lock and lens-reader/bun.lock with `bun install --ignore-scripts`, and moves the version claims inside docs/DEPENDENCIES.md. Every one is a maintenance edit to a hand-authored or tool-owned file rather than a derived artifact: contract-docs-dependencies-md-states-version-pins-in-prose.test.mjs holds the prose to the manifests and the frozen install holds the lockfiles, which are the checks a digest here would duplicate
exempt.tools/photos/pipeline-json.ts: the JSON writer the photo shells drive since 2026-09-15, where jaq was: it writes only what its callers' declarations already cover (src/worker/photo-index.json for add-photos.sh, public/images/metadata.json and the per-stem images/meta/ files for extract-photo-metadata.sh; public/images/hashes.json and public/i/ for hash-thumbnails.sh, whose Python heredoc it replaced on 2026-09-22; src/worker/checkpoints.json for bump-version.sh, the same day and the same way) and mints no artifact of its own, so a declaration here would name the orchestrators' outputs twice
exempt.tools/photos/add-photos.sh: the ORCHESTRATOR rather than a generator: it drives zenc, exif-sooc, hash-thumbnails.sh and gen-alt-text.ts in order, and every artifact that comes out is declared by the script that actually produces it. It also re-bakes the whole library on every run, so it has never been the path that leaves derived data behind
exempt.tools/photos/jxl-originals.ts: writes one key, `jxl`, into src/worker/photo-index.json, and that key is an upload RECEIPT rather than a derivation: it records that a lossless JPEG XL twin decoded back to the R2 original's exact bytes and then went up to R2. Its inputs are the bucket and the network, neither of which a checkout holds, so no digest of committed files could say whether it is stale; the twin's contract test checks every recorded key's shape instead. Same class as add-photos.sh's index write, which is where new photos get their twin
exempt.tools/photos/bump-version.sh: appends one entry to src/worker/checkpoints.json, the deploy-log projection, and writes nothing else. checkpoints:check already diffs that projection against D1 in both directions, which is a stronger claim than a digest of its inputs would be
exempt.tools/photos/reencode-thumbnails.sh: produces public/i/, which is an INPUT to images/histograms, images/fingerprints and images/hashes rather than an output of anything. It is also the exact script whose standalone use caused gotcha 46: it told you to re-run hash-thumbnails.sh and stopped there. derive:check is what now catches a run that re-encodes and skips the re-bake, and the script points at it
exempt.tools/photos/av2-tile-probe.ts: writes 600px tiles, scratch encodes and an optional --json report under the OS temp dir while scoring AV2 or JPEG XL against the shipped AVIF at matched bytes, and commits nothing
exempt.tools/photos/libavif-avm/build.sh: READS public/i/ (one committed 600px tier is the input to its byte-identity gate) and writes only under tools/photos/libavif-avm/build/ and src/, the gitignored AV2 build trees. The shell scanner flags it for mentioning a committed path, which is the over-approximation working as designed
exempt.tools/photos/libavif-avm/simde.ts: writes only under tools/photos/libavif-avm/build/, the gitignored AV2 build tree: rtcd headers, a SIMDe shim, compiled kernel objects, and the libavm.a it appends them to. build.sh --tuned runs it and then gates the result byte for byte against the pristine build, so nothing it writes is ever a committed artifact
exempt.tools/lib/site-config.ts: writes .wrangler.site.jsonc and .wrangler.dev.jsonc, both gitignored: the legacy-shape projections of cloudflare.config.ts + wrangler.config.ts (and of config/dev/, for local dev) for the wrangler commands and the test harness that cannot read the TypeScript config
